project.name: Fleet Planner
project.purpose: Daily tool that fills in Driver and Vehicle columns of an uploaded Excel transport-request file, using a deterministic rules engine plus an optional AI review layer, then exports the same file with only those two columns changed.
project.status: actively developed, core pipeline working and validated against real user data

folder_structure.fleetplanner.db: SQLite database, created at runtime; a real snapshot has also been committed to the linked repo for AI testing purposes
folder_structure.app/db.py: all SQLite schema, migrations, and CRUD
folder_structure.app/rules_parser.py: free-text rule-line recognizer, used ONLY for AI-context notes, not hard rules
folder_structure.app/excel_import.py: daily request-file reader, produces Job objects
folder_structure.app/export.py: writes results into a copy of the original uploaded workbook
folder_structure.app/ui/main_window.py: QMainWindow, tab container, Settings PIN gating
folder_structure.app/ui/plan_day_tab.py: daily workflow screen, largest UI file
folder_structure.app/ui/drivers_tab.py: structured driver hard rules + AI notes
folder_structure.app/ui/vehicles_tab.py: vehicle roster, workshop/exclusion toggle, edit dialog
folder_structure.app/ui/settings_tab.py: API keys, PIN, digest refresh control
folder_structure.app/ui/entity_rules_widget.py: LEGACY, not imported by main_window.py as of last known state, superseded by drivers_tab.py/suppliers_tab.py

modules.responsibility: The deterministic core. No AI, no network calls, fully repeatable. Takes in-memory profiles + jobs, mutates jobs in place.
modules.does_not_import: app.db at module level -- db is passed as an explicit parameter to build_*_profiles functions, keeping this module testable standalone

dataclasses.name: DriverProfile
fields: shift_period ('morning' | 'evening' | None -- replaces shift_start, see HR-002 rework 2026-08-03)
max_working_hours_per_day (hard daily ceiling; None falls back to working_hours_per_day -- new 2026-08-03, replaces the removed MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY module constant)
busy_intervals (RUNTIME, list of (start, end, group_key) tuples -- group_key is the same_driver_key of the job that created that interval, or None)
dataclasses.critical_history_note: shift_start field was OMITTED from this dataclass during an earlier rewrite -- a real bug, fixed, then the field itself was replaced entirely by shift_period on 2026-08-03 (see HR-002 rework in CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 10). Any future field additions to drivers must be added here too, not just in the database.

dataclasses.name: VehicleProfile
fields: in_workshop (bool, merged from db.in_workshop OR db.excluded_from_planning)
busy_intervals (RUNTIME, list of (start, end, group_key) tuples)

dataclasses.name: SupplierHire
dataclasses.computed_property: label -- supplier_name if instance_number==1 else f'{supplier_name} {instance_number-1}'
dataclasses.note: RUNTIME ONLY, created dynamically during allocate(), never stored directly in the database -- only the resulting label text and supplier_id get persisted via finalized_jobs on Finalize

key_functions.name: build_driver_profiles
key_functions.purpose: reads drivers table, skips excluded_from_planning, computes month_overtime_so_far via db.get_driver_month_overtime_hours

key_functions.name: build_supplier_offerings
key_functions.purpose: reads supplier_offerings joined with suppliers, computes cumulative_hours_history via db.get_supplier_cumulative_hours

key_functions.name: _driver_qualifies_for_type
key_functions.purpose: exact-match check against license_types list; returns False entirely if license_types is empty (forces explicit configuration)

key_functions.name: _driver_is_off
key_functions.purpose: weekday check against off_days, with allow_override_days escape hatch

key_functions.name: _job_matches_shift_period
key_functions.purpose: hard rule: True if shift_period is None (no restriction), or if the job is on the correct side of the noon cutoff for 'morning'/'evening'. REFINED 2026-08-09 (Phase 16): only gates a driver's FIRST job of the day, not every job -- takes an optional busy_intervals param; if the driver already has any interval starting on the same calendar date, the window check is skipped entirely (they're already working this day). busy_intervals=None (default) preserves the original always-enforce behavior. Confirmed against a real human-planned file where a 'morning' driver was routinely given an afternoon job as a natural continuation. Threaded through all 7 call sites across the module.

key_functions.name: _overlaps_with_buffer
key_functions.purpose: checks time-interval overlap with a configurable minute buffer (default 0 as of 2026-08-03, was 30 -- see TB-001) for travel time between jobs -- now accepts an ignore_group_key parameter: intervals tagged with that same group_key are skipped, allowing overlap between rows the planner explicitly flagged as belonging to the same 'Same Driver' group.

key_functions.name: _type_matches
key_functions.purpose: case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized EXACT string comparison -- no fuzzy matching, deliberate design choice

key_functions.name: _vehicle_type_needs_vehicle
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, NEW-004 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: False for 'Driver Only' (case-insensitive) -- these rows need a qualified driver but no physical vehicle at all. Confirmed by a real PLANNED.xlsx row. Used across the main pass, gap-filler, and minimum-hours repair pass to skip vehicle-matching entirely for this type; assigned_vehicle_id/plate are left None/blank.

key_functions.name: _merged_hours
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, hour-accounting fix, HR-002 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: Returns the TRUE UNION of hours covered by the given (start, end, ...) intervals -- overlapping or touching intervals count once, not once each. Replaces naive summing everywhere occupied_seconds is read or written (main loop, gap-filler, minimum-hours repair pass) after a real PLANNED.xlsx showed a driver with ~17h 'occupied' (summed) against ~11h true (merged) work, which falsely tripped the daily ceiling. occupied_seconds is now always recomputed via this function immediately after busy_intervals changes, rather than incremented/decremented directly.

key_functions.name: allocate
key_functions.signature: allocate(jobs, drivers, vehicles, supplier_offerings, allowed_driver_ids=None, allowed_supplier_ids=None, allow_override_days=None, travel_buffer_minutes=DEFAULT_TRAVEL_BUFFER_MINUTES)  # 0 as of 2026-08-03, was 30 -- see TB-001
key_functions.algorithm_summary: For each job in time order: try in-house (qualifying + not off + shift period matches (2026-08-09: only gates a driver's FIRST job of a given day, not every job -- see _job_matches_shift_period's entry above) + no overlap + no daily/monthly overtime violation, pick a candidate, then find any free matching vehicle -- or, for a 'Driver Only' row, no vehicle at all, see _vehicle_type_needs_vehicle). Candidate ranking: for a group's SECOND-and-later row, prefer the driver already established for that group (SD-002/SD-003); for a FRESH group's opening row (2026-08-06, SD-005), min(candidates, key=lambda d: d.occupied_seconds + group_total_hours[group_key]) -- projects the group's whole precomputed merged-hours total onto each candidate, not just this one row, so a driver isn't locked into carrying a large event purely because they were idle for its first row; for an UNGROUPED job (2026-08-03, NEW-007) it's specialist-reservation first -- min(candidates, key=lambda d: (-len(d.license_types), d.occupied_seconds)) -- preferring the more broadly-licensed ('generalist') candidate over a narrowly-licensed ('specialist') one, so a driver who is the ONLY qualifier for some vehicle type has their hours reserved for that exclusive work rather than spent on a job a generalist could equally cover. Can't push anyone over their own ceiling since the hard-rule filter already excludes any candidate who'd violate it before either ranking runs. If no in-house driver+vehicle combo found, try supplier: prefer reusing an already-hired unit from today (any matching offering) that's free; if none, hire a new unit from the offering with lowest cumulative_hours_history among those with remaining daily capacity, naming it via SupplierHire.label convention. 'Same Driver' groups (job.same_driver_key): tracks group_drivers/group_vehicle_by_driver/group_supplier_hires registries; prefers reusing the driver/vehicle/supplier-hire already used for that group before considering others, and relaxes the overlap check between rows sharing the same group_key -- BUT (fixed 2026-08-03, SD-004 in the scheduling rules spec) only when the candidate driver's already-established vehicle for that group is the SAME TYPE as what the current row needs (or they have none established yet); otherwise the overlap check runs normally, since a driver can't be on two different vehicles at once just because both rows share a group tag -- a real bug found via a live test (one driver on a Chiller Truck and a Bus simultaneously). Only brings in an additional driver/unit when none of the group's current one(s) still qualify for the next row. shift_period is enforced via _job_matches_shift_period() in the candidate loop (replaces the old exact-time shift_start check, removed 2026-08-03 -- see HR-002 rework). The working-hours check: a blank max_overtime_hours_per_month is treated as 0 overtime allowed (a hard daily cap via working_hours_per_day), not as 'unlimited'. The daily ceiling is now d.max_working_hours_per_day (falls back to working_hours_per_day if blank) instead of the old fixed MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY module constant, which was removed 2026-08-03. All hour arithmetic uses _merged_hours() (2026-08-03 fix, see above), not a running sum. AFTER this per-job loop finishes: _fill_gaps_with_unresolved_jobs() runs once (OPT-002/003, added 2026-08-03 -- NOTE: only covers a driver with a genuine BOUNDED gap, booking before AND after; a driver with wide-open, non-bracketed spare capacity is NOT covered -- see NEW-007, partially resolved by the specialist-reservation fix above but the bounded-gap-only limitation itself is unchanged), THEN _repair_minimum_daily_hours() runs looped up to 5x, sharing one `settled_job_ids` set across all 5 passes (HR-005, 2026-08-03, WIDENED 2026-08-06) -- see each function's own entry below. A real interaction was found 2026-08-03 (Phase 14 predecessor): giving a generalist a single small ungrouped job via the new specialist-reservation ranking, with nothing else to fill their day, can trip HR-005's under-minimum check and get released to unresolved if no one else has room -- turning an assignable-but-short day into unresolved. Not fixed, tied to the open OPT-001 duty-span/unresolved-policy question; now also observed for GROUPED days too since HR-005 can move whole groups (2026-08-06). Deliberately NOT done inside this per-job loop itself: a gap-fill preference was tried directly in candidate selection here first and reverted, since jobs are processed in strict start-time order so the LATER of a gap's two bounding jobs is never assigned yet when an earlier job that would sit in that gap is being considered -- it's structurally impossible for an in-loop check to see that gap. OPEN, raised by the project owner 2026-08-06, not yet diagnosed or resolved: whether the 'Same Driver' reuse-first/lock-in mechanism (SD-002/SD-003) now has too much influence over the final shape of a plan relative to its original 'assist, don't rule' intent, and whether driver selection throughout this function should be driven by an explicit, planner-visible MERIT ranking rather than driver_pool's incidental (alphabetical) list order. See NEXT_SESSION.md Section 5 for the full discussion.
key_functions.note_on_unused_params: allowed_driver_ids and allowed_supplier_ids support a 'restrict to shortlist' feature that has NO UI control yet -- backend-ready, frontend not built

key_functions.name: _driver_has_bounded_gap_fit
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, OPT-002 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: True if job_start/job_end sits strictly BETWEEN one of driver.busy_intervals ending before it and another starting after it (both with the travel buffer) -- i.e. a genuine gap-fill, not merely extending the driver's day earlier or later. Used by _fill_gaps_with_unresolved_jobs() below.

key_functions.name: _fill_gaps_with_unresolved_jobs
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, OPT-002/OPT-003 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: Post-pass, runs once (not looped) right after the main per-job loop, BEFORE _repair_minimum_daily_hours. Confirmed real-world trigger reported by the project owner: a driver got jobs at 13:00-15:00 and 22:00-01:00 (5h work, 7h idle across the 12h span) while a 16:00-20:00 job that fit the gap was left unresolved. For every still-fully-unresolved job (no driver AND no supplier), checks every driver for a bounded gap fit (via _driver_has_bounded_gap_fit) that respects every other hard rule (license/off-day/shift/overlap/ceiling/monthly-cap), and assigns it there instead of leaving it unresolved. Does NOT reclaim a job already given to a supplier -- unwinding a SupplierHire safely is separate, riskier work not attempted. Skips 'Same Driver' grouped jobs.
key_functions.returns: bool -- True if anything was filled (currently unused by the caller, kept for symmetry with _repair_minimum_daily_hours's return value and potential future looping)

key_functions.name: _established_group_vehicle_type
key_functions.added: 2026-08-06, part of the HR-005 widening, Phase 14
key_functions.purpose: Returns the vehicle_type_required already used by this driver for this Same-Driver group (scanning `jobs` group-wide, not just one day), or None if they have no rows in this group yet. Lets the repair pass enforce SD-004 vehicle-type consistency when relocating a whole grouped day onto a new driver, the same way the main allocation loop already does for a group's first assignment.

key_functions.name: _repair_minimum_daily_hours
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, HR-005 in the scheduling rules spec. WIDENED 2026-08-06, Phase 14.
key_functions.purpose: Post-pass hard rule: a driver used at all on a day must reach working_hours_per_day that day. For every (day, driver) left under-minimum, tries to move ALL of that driver's jobs that day to another qualifying driver with room (same license/off-day/shift/overlap/ceiling/monthly-cap checks as the main loop, PLUS SD-004 vehicle-type consistency via _established_group_vehicle_type for grouped jobs); if every job can move, commits the move, else releases the whole day to unresolved with an explicit note. Does not attempt a supplier fallback for a released day (flagged for manual review instead). Best-effort greedy heuristic, not a global optimizer.
key_functions.scope_change_2026_08_06: Previously skipped ANY day containing a 'Same Driver' grouped job entirely -- correct in principle (a group's own hours are sometimes genuinely the shortfall, see the 2026-08-03 refinement below) but on a real day where 84% of rows were grouped, it meant this pass almost never ran at all, leaving severe imbalance unaddressed. Now a grouped day can be moved WHOLE onto one other driver (never split -- the 'same driver' instruction is honored). A `tentative_group_leader`/`tentative_group_vehicle` mechanism within each move-batch prefers keeping a group intact on one new driver, mirroring SD-002/SD-003.
key_functions.bug_fixed_2026_08_03: Phase 11: originally snapshotted every (day, driver)'s job list ONCE at the start and iterated the static snapshot -- a fix for one driver could leave a LATER driver's entry in the same pass reasoning about stale data, causing jobs to visibly ping-pong between two drivers instead of settling (caught by tests/test_gap_filling.py). Fixed by recomputing each pair's actual current jobs/total fresh from `jobs` immediately before processing it. A second latent bug (multiple jobs moved to the same replacement driver in one batch weren't checked against each other's tentative hours/overlap, so two individually-legal moves could jointly exceed a hard rule) was fixed at the same time by tracking tentative per-driver/per-vehicle additions within a batch before anything is committed.
key_functions.bugs_fixed_2026_08_06: Two real bugs found while widening this to move whole groups, caught by tracing driver state against the real UNPLANNED.xlsx before reaching the project owner: (1) THRASHING -- a short group moved onto a driver with room could make that driver's own day look under-minimum to the very next pass, triggering a different group to be moved onto them next, and so on, never settling. Fixed with the new `settled_job_ids` parameter: a set of Python id(job) values shared across all 5 passes of one allocate() call -- once a job is moved, it's added here and never moved again for the rest of that run, trading a little theoretical optimality for a guaranteed stop. (2) PROCESSING-ORDER ARTIFACT -- the search for a new driver picked the first feasible match in driver_pool's natural (alphabetical) order, so a driver who hadn't had their own fix processed YET in the same pass could look 'busy' and lose out to one freed moments earlier by an unrelated move. Fixed by searching candidates in least-occupied-hours-first order instead.
key_functions.returns: bool -- True if anything changed, used by allocate()'s calling loop to decide whether another pass might help

key_functions.name: _unit_driver_feasible
key_functions.purpose: Shared hard-rule feasibility check for a PlanningUnit against a driver, used by allocate_by_merit, allocate_by_anchor, _swap_repair, and the chain search. busy_intervals_override lets a caller check against a hypothetical (reduced or tentatively-extended) interval set instead of the driver's real busy_intervals, without mutating anything.

key_functions.name: _bundle_units_for_driver
key_functions.purpose: Returns every displaceable 'bundle' currently on a driver: each ungrouped unit alone, or a WHOLE Same-Driver group's units together (never split) as one bundle -- matches the same whole-group-move principle _repair_minimum_daily_hours already uses. Smallest-hours-first.

key_functions.name: _bundle_fits_driver
key_functions.purpose: Checks whether an entire bundle could be committed to driver E all together, batch-wise (each unit checked against E's real schedule plus every earlier unit in the same bundle already tentatively placed, so two individually-legal moves can't jointly bust a daily ceiling). start_busy lets the caller check against a hypothetical reduced schedule (used by the chain search to ask 'would this fit if E's own bundle X were moved out of the way first').

key_functions.name: _find_vehicles_for_bundle
key_functions.purpose: Finds a vehicle for every unit in a bundle plan, tracking tentative reservations across the bundle so two units in the same plan don't silently double-book one physical vehicle unless their group tag explicitly allows the overlap.

key_functions.name: _try_place_bundle_chain
key_functions.signature: _try_place_bundle_chain(bundle, units, driver_pool, vehicle_pool, allow_override_days, travel_buffer_minutes, group_vehicle_by_driver, visited_driver_ids, depth_remaining)
key_functions.purpose: Bounded-depth augmenting-path search (same idea as classic bipartite-matching algorithms): finds a legal home for a bundle, either directly, or -- if depth_remaining > 0 -- by displacing one of a candidate driver's own bundles and recursively finding a home for THAT bundle too, chaining through as many drivers as SWAP_REPAIR_CHAIN_DEPTH allows. Each driver visited at most once per chain (visited_driver_ids), so it can never cycle. Returns a list of (bundle, target_driver, plan, vehicle_plan) describing every relocation, or None if no chain works. Purely a search -- nothing mutated until _commit_chain runs.

key_functions.name: _commit_chain
key_functions.purpose: Commits every relocation found by _try_place_bundle_chain, in order: releases every bundle from wherever it's CURRENTLY sitting first (read fresh, never stored ahead of time), then lands every bundle on its new home. The caller must NOT separately pre-release the outermost bundle -- this function already handles that; a real double-release bug (KeyError from reading an already-cleared assigned_driver_id) was found and fixed when _swap_repair briefly did both.

key_functions.name: _swap_repair
key_functions.signature: _swap_repair(units, driver_pool, vehicle_pool, travel_buffer_minutes, allow_override_days, group_drivers, group_vehicle_by_driver, max_rounds=3)
key_functions.purpose: Bounded local search used by allocate_by_anchor (and reusable by other strategies). For each unresolved unit: (1) direct-fit check -- does some qualifying driver already have genuine free room? (2) single-hop -- does displacing one bundle from a driver free room, AND does that bundle then find a legal home elsewhere? (3, added 2026-08-09) multi-hop chain via _try_place_bundle_chain if (2) fails. Never a net-zero shuffle -- every committed move strictly reduces the unresolved count by one.
key_functions.history: 2026-08-06 (Phase 15): single-hop swap of one ungrouped unit only. 2026-08-09 (Phase 16): widened to whole-group/bundle displacement (via _bundle_units_for_driver/_bundle_fits_driver), gained the direct-fit check (a real, separate oversight found via real-data testing -- a driver with genuine free capacity was never being reconsidered), and gained the bounded multi-hop chain search.

key_functions.name: _solver_effective_ceiling_minutes
key_functions.purpose: For allocate_by_solver(): combines the two layered daily-hours checks _unit_driver_feasible() already applies into ONE effective per-driver daily ceiling, in minutes (CP-SAT needs integers). If max_overtime_hours_per_month is blank, the effective ceiling collapses to working_hours_per_day regardless of max_working_hours_per_day (matching the established 'blank monthly overtime = zero daily overtime' precedent); otherwise it's the flat daily ceiling further capped by however much of the monthly budget remains unspent.

key_functions.name: allocate_by_solver
key_functions.signature: allocate_by_solver(jobs, drivers, vehicles, supplier_offerings, allowed_driver_ids=None, allowed_supplier_ids=None, allow_override_days=None, travel_buffer_minutes=DEFAULT_TRAVEL_BUFFER_MINUTES, time_limit_seconds=15.0)
key_functions.purpose: Fourth allocation strategy: Google OR-Tools CP-SAT constraint solver instead of a heuristic. See experimental_allocation_strategies.allocate_by_solver for the full model description, real-data result, disclosed scope boundaries, and bugs found while building it. Requires ortools (lazy import, not a hard app-wide dependency). Not wired into the UI.

modules.fairness_model: hours-occupied, not job-count. min(candidates, key=lambda d: d.occupied_seconds)

supplier_naming_convention.priority: always try to reuse an already-hired unit before hiring a new one, to minimize headcount for the day
supplier_naming_convention.note: user's own historical manually-planned reference files are inconsistent about this numbering (some suppliers numbered, some not) -- confirmed by user this is a manual-entry artifact, NOT the desired behavior; the engine's consistent numbering is correct and should not be changed to match old files

overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_null_or_bla: no overtime allowed at all -- working_hours_per_day becomes a strict daily ceiling (fixed to fail-closed some time ago; this entry was previously stale/wrong here, saying 'unlimited' -- corrected 2026-08-03)
overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_zero: same as blank -- no overtime allowed at all
overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_positive: monthly overtime budget, checked against finalized_jobs history
overtime_model.daily_ceiling: max_working_hours_per_day (per-driver, planner-set, e.g. 12 paired with working_hours_per_day=9). Null/blank falls back to working_hours_per_day (zero daily overtime). Replaces the old fixed MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY module constant, removed 2026-08-03 -- see HR-002 rework.
overtime_model.daily_minimum: NEW 2026-08-03 (HR-005). A driver used at all on a day must reach at least working_hours_per_day that day. Enforced as a post-pass repair (_repair_minimum_daily_hours), not a per-job filter -- see that function's entry above.

confirmed_with_owner: Overlapping times within a flagged group are allowed for the same driver (not a conflict).
No hard-coded time-based or vehicle-type-based split -- fewest additional drivers/units possible, via reuse-first preference.
same_driver_group_feature.hour_accounting: occupied_seconds and monthly overtime projection use the TRUE UNION of a driver's intervals (_merged_hours()), not a naive sum -- two same-group rows that overlap in time (e.g. two simultaneous pickups on one truck) count once. This entry previously said hours were still SUMMED here -- that was stale/wrong left over from before the Phase 12 hour-accounting fix (2026-08-03); corrected 2026-08-06.
same_driver_group_feature.group_leader_selection: A fresh group's opening row picks its driver by projecting the group's TOTAL merged hours onto each candidate (SD-005, added 2026-08-06, Phase 14), not just the opening row's own duration -- see allocate()'s algorithm_summary above. Fixed a real hour-imbalance bug where a driver idle for one instant could end up carrying an entire large event alone.
same_driver_group_feature.open_concern_2026_08_06_RESOLVED_INTO_AL: The project owner's concern (SD-002/SD-003's reuse-first/lock-in possibly having too much influence, plus a separate merit-based-selection idea) was resolved not by patching this mechanism directly, but by building two full alternative strategies alongside allocate() for real comparison: allocate_by_merit() and allocate_by_anchor() (see the top-level 'experimental_allocation_strategies' entry below and CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 15). allocate()'s own SD-002/SD-003 logic was NOT changed.
tested_with: real UNPLANNED.xlsx + fleetplanner.db (all 9 real flagged groups resolved correctly, 2026-08-03; re-validated 2026-08-06 for the HR-005 widening, see Phase 14)

idle_driver_rescue.purpose: Makes 'every driver has real work' a first-class goal, not just 'no driver is illegally under-minimum' -- confirmed by directly comparing real output to the real PLANNED.xlsx (which uses all 11 drivers, none below 7.5h) and finding both allocate() and allocate_by_merit() left 2 drivers at a legal-but-unrealistic 0h, usually a side effect of _repair_minimum_daily_hours freeing a short day to fix someone else's minimum, never revisited afterward. For every 0h driver, tentatively accumulates candidates (unresolved jobs first, then genuine surplus from other drivers -- hours above THEIR OWN minimum, never dropping a donor below it) and only commits to real state if the FULL total clears the idle driver's own minimum; otherwise everything tentative is discarded for free.
idle_driver_rescue.bugs_fixed_2026_08_06: Two real bugs found via the EXISTING test suite (tests/test_daily_overtime_ceiling.py), not new tests, before either reached the project owner: (1) a genuinely-unfixable released job got rescued right back onto the exact driver it was correctly released from, because the first version committed the first feasible candidate without checking the FULL accumulated total against the minimum -- fixed with the all-or-nothing tentative-then-commit design described above. (2) a donor's 'remaining hours after removal' calculation excluded their already-settled jobs from the baseline entirely, making them look like they'd drop to a legal 0h when they'd actually be left with an illegal short day -- fixed by using two separate lists: the donor's TRUE full current workload for the remaining-hours check, and a narrower 'pullable' list (excluding settled jobs) for what's actually eligible to move.

important_constants_in_this_module.MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY: REMOVED 2026-08-03. Was 2.0, a hard per-day overtime ceiling on top of working_hours_per_day, global/not per-driver configurable. Replaced by the per-driver DriverProfile.max_working_hours_per_day field -- see HR-002 rework, CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 10.
important_constants_in_this_module.SHIFT_PERIOD_EVENING_CUTOFF_HOUR: NEW 2026-08-03. Currently 12 (noon) -- the hour-of-day boundary _job_matches_shift_period() uses to decide morning vs evening. A single global constant, not per-driver configurable, since the planner only asked for a simple morning/evening split.

business_rules: In-house drivers/vehicles are always attempted before any supplier for every job, independently, in time order -- no pre-reservation of jobs for suppliers.
Fairness among in-house drivers is measured by cumulative occupied HOURS, not job count.
A driver's license_types must contain an EXACT (case/whitespace-normalized) match for a job's vehicle_type_required, or the driver is not considered at all for that job.

A job's time-of-day must match a driver's shift_period ('morning'=before 12:00, 'evening'=12:00 onward, None=no restriction) -- but ONLY for a driver's FIRST job of a given day (refined 2026-08-09, confirmed against a real human-planned file: a 'morning' driver routinely continued into the afternoon as a natural extension of a day already under way). Once a driver has any job on a date, later jobs that day are governed purely by normal overlap/hour-ceiling rules, not re-checked against the shift window. Replaces the old exact-time shift_start model 2026-08-03 -- the planner no longer fixes an exact clock time before planning, just a Morning/Evening label; no automatic rotation. See HR-002 rework and the 2026-08-09 first-job-only refinement (CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 16).
Off days are a hard skip unless explicitly overridden for a specific date (allow_override_days parameter, no UI yet).
max_overtime_hours_per_month: NULL/blank = no overtime allowed at all (same as 0); positive number = monthly budget checked against finalized_jobs history.
Supplier hiring always tries to REUSE an already-hired unit before hiring a new one, to minimize the day's headcount, even if it means one supplier driver works more hours.
New supplier hires are chosen from the offering with the LOWEST cumulative historical hours among suppliers with remaining daily capacity, for cross-day fairness.

Supplier unit naming: 1st hire = bare supplier name, 2nd hire = 'NAME 1', Nth = 'NAME {N-1}', reuse = 'SAME <label>'. This is user-confirmed and should not be changed based on old inconsistent manual reference files.
A vehicle is unavailable if EITHER in_workshop OR excluded_from_planning is set -- they are treated as equivalent for allocation purposes.
AI suggestions never change the plan automatically -- every suggestion requires an explicit planner Accept/Reject click.

The raw decision_log is never sent to Claude -- only the small, periodically-refreshed preference_digest is included in daily AI Review calls, to keep cost/latency flat over time regardless of history length.
Export must preserve the original uploaded file exactly, changing only the Vehicle and Driver cell values for matched rows -- no reformatting, no regeneration from a template.
Unresolved jobs (no valid assignment found) are never written to finalized_jobs.
Events (grouped by event_id) with 2+ stages are the unit of reasoning for the AI's stay-on-site-vs-cycle-back judgment; single-stage events are excluded from that reasoning entirely.

The 'Same Driver' Excel column lets the planner flag rows that should be handled by one driver back-and-forth; overlapping times within such a flagged group are allowed for the same driver, and the engine brings in the fewest additional drivers/supplier units possible rather than a hard-coded time or vehicle-type split.
A blank 'Max overtime/month' for a driver is treated the same as an explicit 0 (no overtime allowed) -- working_hours_per_day still applies as a hard daily cap in that case.

License-type qualification (a driver must hold the exact vehicle type license for a job) was audited at the project owner's request in an earlier session and confirmed correctly enforced -- no bug found here.

A driver's daily ceiling is max_working_hours_per_day (planner-set per driver, e.g. 12), on top of working_hours_per_day, regardless of remaining monthly overtime budget. Replaces the old fixed, global MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY=2.0 constant 2026-08-03 -- see HR-002 rework. Blank falls back to working_hours_per_day (zero daily overtime).

NEW 2026-08-03 (HR-005): a driver used at all on a day must reach at least working_hours_per_day that day (hard minimum, not just a target). Enforced as a post-allocation repair pass, not a per-job filter, since the engine can't know a day's total until its last job is considered -- see allocation_engine._repair_minimum_daily_hours.

NEW 2026-08-06: max_working_hours_per_day left blank means the ceiling EQUALS working_hours_per_day itself (a fixed day, not a range) -- confirmed against the real PLANNED.xlsx, where the only drivers landing at exactly their working_hours_per_day are precisely the ones with no max configured. See _driver_ceiling() in allocation_engine.py.

NEW 2026-08-06: 'every driver has real work' is now a first-class goal alongside the existing hard rules -- a driver left at a legal-but-unrealistic 0h is actively rescued if genuine surplus or unresolved work can bring them to their OWN minimum without creating a new violation anywhere else. See _rebalance_idle_drivers().

experimental_allocation_strategies.added: 2026-08-06 (Phase 15), substantially extended 2026-08-09 (Phase 16) -- see CHANGELOG_AI.md and NEXT_SESSION.md Section 5/6
experimental_allocation_strategies.status: NOT wired into the UI. plan_day_tab.py calls only allocate(). Built alongside it for real-data comparison, per Rule 13 -- never assume any of the three newer strategies has replaced allocate() without checking main_window.py/plan_day_tab.py imports first. As of Phase 16 (2026-08-09), allocate_by_anchor() and the new allocate_by_solver() both independently reach 0 unresolved / 0 supplier / all 11 drivers used on the real UNPLANNED.xlsx -- allocate_by_solver()'s result is additionally a PROVEN-optimal status, not just a found solution.
experimental_allocation_strategies.trigger: The project owner raised two structural concerns after Phase 14: 'Same Driver' grouping felt like it was ruling the allocation rather than assisting it (though removing it entirely made a real day WORSE, 12 unresolved, confirming it's genuinely load-bearing), and driver selection was effectively alphabetical in places rather than merit-based.

shared_infrastructure.PlanningUnit: dataclass wrapping 1 or 2 Job objects (jobs, start_dt, end_dt, vehicle_type_required, same_driver_key, event_id). Both new strategies operate on units instead of raw jobs.
shared_infrastructure.build_planning_units(jobs): Pairs-only pre-merge: two Same-Driver rows sharing a vehicle type and start/end within 1h become one internal unit BEFORE allocation runs, instead of being handled via allocate()'s runtime overlap-relaxation machinery. Never merges 3+ rows into one unit -- a 3rd row in a cluster falls through to ordinary handling. Export always shows original rows separately.

allocate_by_merit.design: Shift-partition (morning/evening pools) -> event-diversified seeding (prefer a NEW event over a 2nd job from an event someone else already started; license scarcity always overrides seeding and takes the job immediately) -> merit fill (least-occupied-first, specialist-reservation tiebreak) -> supplier fallback -> rearrangement loop.
allocate_by_merit.real_data_result: 16 unresolved vs. baseline's 12 -- WORSE. The aggressive event-diverse seeding spends driver availability faster than the rearrangement stage can recover it. Disclosed as underperforming, not hidden or oversold.

allocate_by_anchor.design: Shift-partition -> for each driver, MOST-CONSTRAINED (narrowest license_types) first: anchor their FIRST job (earliest available), compute target finish (first job's end + their ceiling via _driver_ceiling()), anchor a LAST job (whichever remaining job ends closest to, but not after, that target) -> middle fill (least-occupied-first) -> bounded swap-repair (_swap_repair, capped rounds, default 3 -- only commits a swap if the displaced job finds a legal new home, never a net-zero shuffle) -> supplier fallback -> rearrangement loop. (2026-08-09, Phase 16): _swap_repair widened to displace whole Same-Driver-group bundles (not just single ungrouped jobs), gained a direct-fit check tried before any displacement, and gained a bounded multi-hop chain search (_try_place_bundle_chain, SWAP_REPAIR_CHAIN_DEPTH=2) for cases where every driver is individually blocked but only because each is blocking someone else. The outer loop was also restructured to alternate the rearrangement stage and swap-repair (up to 10 rounds) instead of running swap-repair only once before rearrangement, so a job released by a LATER rearrangement pass still gets a swap attempt.
allocate_by_anchor.real_data_result: 2026-08-06: 12 unresolved, tied with baseline, but 9/9 active drivers had real work vs. baseline's 9/11 with 2 fully idle. 2026-08-09 (Phase 16), after widening _swap_repair (whole-group/bundle displacement, a direct-fit check, a bounded multi-hop chain search) and correcting the shift-window rule to gate only a driver's first job of the day: 0 unresolved, 0 supplier, all 11 drivers used -- matching allocate_by_solver()'s headline result via a different (heuristic, not provably-optimal) approach.
allocate_by_anchor.bug_fixed_2026_08_06: Supplier-fallback branches set assigned_supplier_unit but forgot to reset job.unresolved back to False (a leftover from provisionally marking every pre-swap leftover unit unresolved) -- successfully-supplied jobs were silently still counted as unresolved. Fixed by adding the missing reset in both the reuse and new-hire commit paths.

experimental_allocation_strategies.test_coverage_gap: None of allocate_by_merit, allocate_by_anchor, _swap_repair, or build_planning_units have dedicated synthetic test files yet -- all validation so far is direct real-data testing against UNPLANNED.xlsx + fleetplanner.db. This is a real, disclosed gap flagged in NEXT_SESSION.md, not an oversight.

allocate_by_solver.design: Fundamentally different from the other three: instead of a hand-written heuristic, states every hard rule as a constraint and the real goal as a weighted objective in Google OR-Tools' CP-SAT solver, which searches the space directly and provably. Decision variables: x[unit,driver] (license-compatible pairs only), veh[unit,vehicle] (type-compatible pairs only), unresolved[unit]. Hard constraints: exactly one of {one driver, unresolved} per unit; a vehicle iff a driver (none for 'Driver Only' rows); no two time-overlapping units share a driver or vehicle; shift window as a first-job-only gate via has_morning/has_evening linking variables per driver; daily ceiling folding in the monthly-overtime-budget interaction (_solver_effective_ceiling_minutes); daily floor WITH the same Same-Driver-group exemption _repair_minimum_daily_hours already has. Soft preference (objective term, not a hard rule): Same-Driver group cohesion via touches_group[group,driver] (minimize distinct drivers per group -- NOT pairwise together[i,j,driver], which was tried first and caused a 60x+ slowdown). Warm-started via model.add_hint() from a fast allocate_by_anchor() run on scratch copies, purely as a starting point. Objective: 1,000,000 x unresolved_count + 10,000 x group_driver_touches + unused_capacity_among_used_drivers - used_driver_bonus. Supplier hiring is NOT modeled inside the solver -- whatever it leaves unresolved is run through the exact same reuse-before-hire logic allocate()'s supplier pass already uses, copied not reimplemented.
allocate_by_solver.real_data_result: 44/44 resolved, 0 supplier hires, all 11 drivers used, solver status PROVEN OPTIMAL (CP-SAT's branch-and-bound genuinely proves no better in-house assignment exists under the modeled constraints, not just 'a solution was found'), 3.78 seconds wall time. Matches the real human-planned ground truth's own headline result (44/44, 0 supplier, all 11 drivers), though not the identical per-driver hour distribution -- expected, more than one valid way exists to reach 44/44.
disclosed_scope_boundaries: Genuine time-overlap relaxation for Same-Driver group members beyond what build_planning_units() already pre-merges into exact pairs is NOT modeled -- if two different units share a same_driver_key AND genuinely overlap in time, ordinary overlap rules apply here and they can never legally land on the same driver, even though the other three strategies' SD-004-aware relaxation would allow it for a matching vehicle type. The dominant real pattern (two simultaneous same-vehicle pickups) is unaffected, since pre-merging already handles that as one decision.

Supplier hiring is not modeled inside the solver itself -- dynamically naming/numbering hired units the way the solver would need to is a materially different combinatorial problem; the existing supplier pass is reused unchanged instead.
bugs_found_while_building: OR-Tools' deprecated camelCase model.AddHint(...) has a broken compatibility shim with list arguments in the pinned ortools version (9.15) -- raises a confusing TypeError deep inside the library. The real, current method is snake_case model.add_hint(var, value), called once per (variable, value) pair, not with lists.

A first, logically-correct pairwise together[unit_i,unit_j,driver] encoding for the Same-Driver group-cohesion soft preference measurably slowed the solver -- proven-optimal in well under a second cold, versus over 60 seconds (status FEASIBLE, not OPTIMAL) with this encoding added, because pairwise terms create a lot of symmetric, equally-good alternatives. Replaced with the leaner touches_group[group,driver] encoding (O(members) instead of O(members^2) per group).

The solver's first version of the daily-floor constraint hadn't replicated the existing Same-Driver-group exemption _repair_minimum_daily_hours already has (a driver whose whole day is grouped work isn't forced to hit the floor). Confirmed as a real gap via the real ground-truth file's own VISWANADHAN (5.0h, well under his 9h floor, entirely inside one flagged group) -- fixed by making the floor constraint's enforcement conditional on used[driver] AND NOT has_grouped_unit[driver].
allocate_by_solver.requires: The 'ortools' package (added to requirements.txt), imported LAZILY inside the function so the rest of the app -- including the other three strategies -- works with zero impact if it isn't installed.
allocate_by_solver.not_wired_into_ui: plan_day_tab.py still calls only allocate(). See NEXT_SESSION.md Section 6 item 2 for the open sub-questions.

workflows.name: daily_planning_workflow
steps: 1. Upload Excel file -> excel_import.load_jobs_from_excel -> list[Job] in memory
3. Run Planning -> allocation_engine.allocate() mutates jobs -> results table rendered, filter dropdown populated
4. (optional) AI Review -> travel-time lookups via maps_client + db.resolve_location -> ai_review.review_plan() -> suggestion cards with Accept/Reject
5. (per suggestion) Accept/Reject -> db.log_decision (does NOT auto-update the table -- known gap)
6. Finalize Day -> db.save_finalized_jobs (skips unresolved jobs, overwrites existing rows for that date)
7. Export Filled Excel -> export.export_filled_excel writes into a COPY of the original file, saved wherever the planner chooses

workflows.name: digest_refresh_workflow
workflows.trigger: manual, planner clicks 'Refresh Preferences Digest Now' in Settings tab
steps: 1. db.get_digest -> existing digest text + covered_through_date watermark
3. If none new: return existing digest unchanged, ZERO API calls made
4. If new decisions exist: send existing digest + new decisions to Claude, get merged/updated digest text (capped ~400 words)
5. db.save_digest with new watermark = latest decision's plan_date

workflows.name: master_data_setup_workflow
workflows.description: one-time-ish setup, edited only when something changes (new driver, rate change, vehicle to workshop)

architectural_decisions.decision: Standalone single-user desktop app, not multi-user web app
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Only one planner uses the actual software; supervisor/drivers only ever see the exported file distributed externally. Eliminated need for hosting/accounts/real-time sync entirely.

architectural_decisions.decision: Deterministic engine and AI review are two separate, manually-triggered steps, not automatically combined
architectural_decisions.reasoning: While the deterministic engine was (and still is, to some degree) being actively debugged, keeping AI out of the automatic loop made every discovered issue traceable to one layer or the other. A combined one-click shortcut is a deliberately deferred future addition.

architectural_decisions.decision: AI never finalizes anything automatically -- suggestions require explicit Accept/Reject
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Non-negotiable requirement from the first design discussion; human stays in control of every change.

architectural_decisions.decision: Two-tier decision history: full local log (never sent) + small periodically-refreshed digest (only thing sent)
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Answers 'does the AI learn over time' honestly (the model is stateless per call) while letting the SYSTEM reflect accumulated real decisions without unbounded cost/latency growth.

architectural_decisions.decision: Hard rules moved from free-text rule-line parsing to structured database columns
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Directly caused by two real bugs (a driver's hour cap silently unenforced due to un-matched phrasing; later, shift_start type of issue) where free-text matching failed silently. Structured fields with explicit format-hint UI eliminate the ambiguity.

architectural_decisions.decision: Supplier units are generated dynamically at planning time, never pre-named by the planner
architectural_decisions.reasoning: The original 'pre-name your trucks' model was identified as backwards -- the app should decide unit numbering based on actual daily demand, not have the planner guess in advance.

architectural_decisions.decision: Export loads and modifies the ORIGINAL workbook rather than regenerating from a template
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Explicit requirement: output must be byte-identical to the input except for the Vehicle/Driver cells -- no reformatting risk.

architectural_decisions.decision: Settings PIN disables the tab entirely rather than switch-then-revert
architectural_decisions.reasoning: The switch-then-revert approach could flash tab contents before the check completed -- a real, observed issue, fixed by disabling the tab outright while locked.

architectural_decisions.decision: Additive-only schema migrations (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN)
architectural_decisions.reasoning: After multiple rounds of asking the user to delete their local database for schema changes, this was added so small future field additions don't cause data loss. Structural changes (rename/retype/remove) still require a fresh database.

architectural_decisions.decision: Vehicle-type matching is exact string comparison, never fuzzy
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Deliberately rejected fuzzy matching as riskier than the problem it solves (risk of silently conflating genuinely different vehicle configurations). Real-world text mismatches are treated as a data-entry/process problem to fix at the source, not a matching-algorithm problem to work around.

important_constants.name: DEFAULT_TRAVEL_BUFFER_MINUTES
important_constants.changed_2026_08_03: was 30. Confirmed with the project owner (TB-001 in the scheduling rules spec): a planner-set end time already accounts for travel back to base -- e.g. 05:00-08:00 followed by 08:00-11:00 for the same driver is intentional, 08:00 IS the chosen return-to-base time, not a shorthand needing a buffer added on top. A non-zero buffer was double-counting travel time already built into the planner's chosen times and blocking real back-to-back continuations between unrelated orders. Re-running a full real-file reconstruction after this change took it from 42/44 to 44/44 rows auto-assigned. FUTURE WORK: once live Google Maps travel-time lookups are wired in, gaps between jobs at genuinely different locations should be checked against real drive time instead of trusting manual timing -- a distance-aware replacement for this flat constant, not a reason to raise it back to a flat non-zero value in the meantime.
important_constants.purpose: minimum gap enforced between two jobs assigned to the same driver or vehicle; 0 means adjacent/zero-gap jobs are allowed, only genuine time overlap is a conflict

important_constants.name: MAX_DIGEST_WORDS
important_constants.purpose: caps preference_digest size regardless of how much history feeds into it

important_constants.name: DEFAULT_DB_PATH
important_constants.value: next to the app directory, fleetplanner.db

important_constants.name: SHIFT_PERIOD_EVENING_CUTOFF_HOUR
important_constants.purpose: hour-of-day boundary for morning vs evening shift_period. Replaces MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY (removed 2026-08-03) at this spot in the constants list -- the daily overtime ceiling is now the per-driver max_working_hours_per_day field, not a module constant. See HR-002 rework.

important_constants.name: SWAP_REPAIR_CHAIN_DEPTH
important_constants.purpose: Bounded depth for _try_place_bundle_chain()'s multi-hop augmenting-path search inside _swap_repair (added 2026-08-09, Phase 16). Each driver visited at most once per chain, so search is always bounded by min(depth, len(driver_pool)) and can never cycle.

The HR-005 daily-minimum-hours repair pass (added 2026-08-03, Phase 10): a staleness bug was found and fixed 2026-08-03 (Phase 11) after a live-test report, and it was refined 2026-08-03 (Phase 12) after a real PLANNED.xlsx showed the total-hours check needed to include a driver's grouped-job hours too, not just ungrouped ones. WIDENED 2026-08-06 (Phase 14) to move whole grouped days instead of skipping them entirely, after real data showed the 'skip grouped days' scope was defeating this pass almost completely on a day where 84% of rows were grouped. Two more real bugs (thrashing between drivers, and a processing-order artifact in driver search) were found and fixed the same day. Real-data spread went from 2.0h-16.0h to 4.0h-11.0h against a 5.0h-12.0h human-planned reference -- real progress, not yet full parity. See CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 14.

OPT-002/003 gap-filling (added 2026-08-03, Phase 11): fixes the confirmed real-world case of a driver ending up with a wide idle gap while a job that fit the gap was left unresolved. Does not reclaim jobs already given to a supplier. Validated against a full real day's reconstruction 2026-08-03 (Phase 12), not just synthetic scenarios -- see CHANGELOG_AI.md.

OPEN, not decided (spec OPT-001): should a driver's duty SPAN (first job to last job, including idle time) count toward daily/monthly hour limits, instead of summed job duration as today? RESOLVED 2026-08-06 into two real alternative strategies, not a patch to allocate() (see the 'experimental_allocation_strategies' entry above and CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 15): the 2026-08-06 question about Same Driver's influence and merit-based selection led to allocate_by_merit() and allocate_by_anchor() being built alongside allocate(). Neither is wired into the UI yet, and neither has beaten the baseline outright -- allocate_by_anchor ties on unresolved count with better driver utilization; allocate_by_merit underperforms. A decision on next steps (keep tuning, add tests, or pause) is still needed from the project owner.

FIXED 2026-08-06 (was open as NEW-008): the embedded-newline data bug was NOT isolated to one driver -- found in all 11 active drivers' license_types, one vehicle's vehicle_type (plate Z 43915), and two excluded drivers (15 records total). Fixed with a direct SQL sweep, confirmed clean with a follow-up scan across drivers.license_types/vehicles.vehicle_type/supplier_offerings.vehicle_type. Real result: 2 of 3 affected rows now resolve correctly, but total unresolved count did not drop overall (ticked up slightly) -- the honest signature of a greedy heuristic reshuffling around new legal options, not a new bug. Confirms the remaining gap to zero-unresolved is now an algorithm limit, not a data problem.

CONFIRMED 2026-08-06, not fixable in software: the 10-Ton-Chiller-Truck scarcity contributing to unresolved rows is a genuine capacity constraint -- only one physical vehicle of that type exists (plate A 67338), and no supplier offers that exact type either. Flagged to the project owner as a real gap to close (a second vehicle, or a matching supplier offering) if they want fewer unresolved rows of this specific type -- not something to work around in code.
